delete_target_only_condition_sets.description: Only applies to copying into an existing environment. Delete the target environment's condition sets whose key the source environment does not have and that `scope` selects (with the same matching as the copy), together with their rules; a resource set is selected only when its resource is copied. Autogenerated condition sets are never deleted, and the copy fails with 409 instead of deleting a condition set that has a descendant which would not itself be deleted. Requires permission to delete condition sets in the target; in a policy-guarded target a guarded condition set is not deleted (the copy fails with 403, or 503 if the guard cannot be reached). Off by default: without it, neither conflict strategy deletes condition sets

audience.description: The audience an Elements user JWT's 'aud' claim must contain; with a list, a token naming at least one of them is accepted. When set, a token minted for any other audience is rejected. Setting it alone does not check the issuer: on Entra ID set `issuer` too, or a token another tenant issued for this audience is accepted. Cognito access tokens carry no 'aud' (they carry `client_id`), so only Cognito ID tokens pass when it is set. Required on the same shared-host and Firebase Auth configs as `issuer` (see its description). An update whose `jwks` omits it keeps the stored value; send null to clear it.
audience.title: Audience

issuer.description: The 'iss' claim an Elements user JWT must carry, compared exactly (an Auth0 issuer ends in '/'); with a list, a token from any one of them is accepted. When set, a token from any other issuer is rejected. Set it, together with `audience`, whenever the JWKS's keys also sign tokens for other applications: Entra ID (any `login.microsoftonline.com` JWKS URL, tenant-specific ones included, because Entra's signing keys are shared by every tenant), Google, Apple, or an Auth0 or Cognito tenant other applications use. For a `url` on one of those shared hosts (Entra, Google, Apple, Salesforce, LinkedIn, Facebook) both are required when the config is created or its `url` is set or changed, and by an update that leaves `user_key_claim` set and changes it, this or `audience`. On Firebase Auth's JWKS (any URL whose last path segment is `securetoken@system.gserviceaccount.com` or `sessionCookiePublicKeys`, in any case) both are required on those writes, and Elements login and invite approval are refused until both are set: `issuer` 'https://securetoken.google.com/<project-id>' (session cookies: 'https://session.firebase.google.com/<project-id>') and `audience` '<project-id>'. A value left unset is taken from the token itself, so it checks nothing. An update whose `jwks` omits it keeps the stored value; send null to clear it.
issuer.title: Issuer

user_key_claim.description: The claim of an Elements user JWT whose value is the Permit user key; unset means 'sub'. Elements login and invite approval read the user key from this claim only: a request's own `user_key_claim` is accepted only when omitted, 'sub', or equal to this one, and is otherwise rejected. The claim's value must be a non-empty string or an integer (read as its decimal string; a boolean, or a number with a fraction or exponent, is rejected); 'email' is accepted only from a token whose 'email_verified' is the JSON boolean true (that check applies only to a claim named exactly 'email'; tokens without 'email_verified', such as Entra ID's, or with the string 'true', as Sign in with Apple has sent, cannot use it, and an email-keyed user changes key when the IdP email changes). Name only a claim your IdP sets: claims the end user or the client can set (an OIDC 'nonce', 'name', 'aud', ...) are refused, and a custom claim filled from metadata the user can edit is just as unsafe. An update whose `jwks` omits it keeps the stored value; send null to clear it. On a shared IdP host (Entra ID, Google, ...), an update that leaves it set and changes it, `issuer` or `audience` needs both of those set, so neither can be cleared while it is set. Removing the whole config (`jwks: null`) removes it too, so a config created again keys users on 'sub' until it is set again.
user_key_claim.title: User Key Claim

keys.description: The keys to match against the request headers: public keys only. A key carrying a private member (`d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `oth`, `k`), or a symmetric `oct` key, is refused on write, except that an update may send back a key exactly as stored. Reads show each key without those members and leave `oct` keys out.
keys.title: Keys

data_generator_lib__schemas__schema_opal.description:
This is the data structure that is used by the PDP in a manged Permit environment.
The code Permit generates uses this data structure to enforce the policy and make decisions.

condition_set_rules.description:
Key-Value mapping of the permissions for each condition set.
The key is the user-set key and the value is Key-Value mapping of resource-set key to the permissions for that user-set & resource-set.The key is the resource key and the value is list of actions that the user-set can perform on that resource-set
condition_set_rules.title: Condition Set Rules

condition_set_rules_expand.description:
Sanitized Key-Value mapping of the permissions for each condition set.
(Equal to condition_set_rules but user_set_key and resource_set_key are sanitized)The key is the user-set key and the value is Key-Value mapping of resource-set key to the permissions for that user-set & resource-set.The key is the resource key and the value is list of actions that the user-set can perform on that resource-set
condition_set_rules_expand.title: Condition Set Rules Expand

condition_sets.description:
Key-Value mapping of the condition sets in the system.
The key is the formatted condition set key and the value contains some details about the condition set.
condition_sets.title: Condition Sets

mapping_rules.description:
Key-Value mapping of groups of mapping rules in the system.
The key is the mapping rule group and the value is a list of mapping rules objects.We currently have only one group named 'all' which contains all the mapping rules.A mapping rule object contains, action, http_method, resource and url - all strings.
mapping_rules.title: Mapping Rules

relationships.description:
Key-Value mapping of the relationships between resources.
The key is the resource instance key and the value is Key-Value mapping of relation key to a Key-Value mapping of resource ( type ) to list of instances keys.
relationships.title: Relationships

resource_instances.description:
Key-Value mapping of the resource instances in the system.
The key is the resource instance key and the value contains some details about the resource instance.
resource_instances.title: Resource Instances

resource_types.description:
Key-Value mapping of the resource types in the system.
The key is the resource type key and the value contains some details about the resource type.
resource_types.title: Resource Types

role_assignments.description:
Key-Value mapping of the role assignments for the users.
The key is the user key and the value is Key-Value mapping of resource instance key or tenant key to list of role keys assigned to the user in that resource instance.
role_assignments.title: Role Assignments

role_permissions.description:
Key-Value mapping of the permissions for each role.
The key is the resource key and the value is Key-Value mapping of role key to details on the role permissions.
role_permissions.title: Role Permissions

roles.description:
Key-Value mapping of the roles in the system.
The key is the role key and the value contains some details about the role.
roles.title: Roles

tenants.description:
Key-Value mapping of the tenants in the system.
The key is the tenant key and the value contains some details about the tenant.
tenants.title: Tenants

users.description:
Key-Value mapping of the users in the system.
The key is the user key and the value contains some details about the user.
users.title: Users

(one `data/<table>.csv` per table + `manifest.json`).

Requires an Organization API key with ADMIN access; write/read-only keys are
rejected. The organization is taken from the key, so this only ever exports
your own organization. The archive contains your plaintext API-key secrets
(so a self-hosted import keeps working without re-issuing keys) — treat the
download URL and the file as credentials.

403.description: The API key lacks ADMIN access to the organization — the archive contains every plaintext API-key secret, so a write/read-only key is rejected (same gate as GET /v2/api-key/{id})

503.description: Export storage is not configured — try again later

presigned `download_url`; on `failure` the `error` explains why (e.g. the
org is too large for the self-service export). Only exports of your own
organization are visible.

delete.description:
Removes a user from the element's scope.

In a tenant element, the user leaves the caller's tenant with everything they hold in
it: their membership, their tenant-level roles and their roles on the tenant's resource
instances (404 if they are not a member). In a ReBAC element, only their roles on the
`resource_instance_id` instance are removed (400 if no instance is named, 404 if they
hold no role on it), and their membership in the tenant goes with their last role in it.

Every role about to be removed is rated with this element's levels first: 403 when the
element hides one, or when a LEVEL_2 caller would remove a LEVEL_1 role. A role this
element does not configure stays removable.

The user is then deleted from the environment if they hold no role or membership in
any tenant.

- If the `tenant` filter is present, will only return the role assignments in that tenant (supports multiple).
- If the `role` filter is present, will only return role assignments that are granting that role (supports multiple).

If multiple tenants are received, the last tenant will be compared with the resource instance.

if such org exists and can be accessed by the authenticated actor.

delete.description:
Schedules an organization (Permit.io account) for permanent deletion.

Effective immediately, the organization disappears from `GET /v2/orgs`
(list) and direct lookups (`GET /v2/orgs/{id}`); subsequent `PATCH` and
`DELETE` calls on it return 404. To preserve recoverability during the
grace period, member grants and existing API keys are intentionally
retained — support can restore the organization until the cutoff is
reached. After the grace period the organization and all of its data
are permanently removed.

**Contract change:** This endpoint previously returned `204 No Content`
with an empty body and an immediate hard-delete. It now returns
`202 Accepted` with a JSON body describing when the permanent deletion
will occur. Existing clients that branched on `status == 204` need to be
updated.

An organization with an environment protected by a policy guard is not scheduled: the
request is refused with 403, for every caller, until an organization admin deletes the
policy guard scope (which un-guards every environment of the organization).

Error responses are documented in the OpenAPI ``responses`` block above.

parameters.description: Either the unique id of the organization, or the URL-friendly key of the organization (i.e: the "slug").
parameters.name: org_id

schema.description: Either the unique id of the organization, or the URL-friendly key of the organization (i.e: the "slug").
schema.title: Org Id

403.description: Nothing is scheduled. The caller may not delete the organization, or one of its environments is protected by a policy guard: then no caller can delete the organization, with error code `POLICY_GUARD_PROTECTED`, until an organization admin deletes the policy guard scope (creating one first if the organization has none)

404.description: Organization not found, or already scheduled for deletion.

409.description: Concurrent deletion request detected (race between two callers).

post.description:
Restores a soft-deleted organization. Superuser-only endpoint.

Clears the deleted_at timestamp so the organization becomes visible again.
UUID-only: slug lookup is not accepted because org keys are only unique
among active orgs (partial unique index on `key WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`).
Idempotent: calling restore on an already-active org returns the current row.
Returns 403 if the caller is not a superuser.
Returns 404 if no organization with the given id exists.
Returns 409 if another active org has reused this org's key while it was
soft-deleted — the key must be freed before this org can be restored.
Returns 422 if org_id is not a valid UUID.

post.description:
The migration process is as followed:
1. Perform request to this endpoint with the new number of shards
2. A new PDP Config will be created with the new number of shards and a new api-key
3. Create a new PDP cluster with the same instances as the number of shards defined in the new PDP Config
4. Wait for the new PDP cluster to be ready
5. Update your PDP load balancer to point to the new PDP cluster

More info can be found here https://docs.permit.io/concepts/pdp-sharding

post.description:
Triggers an out-of-band data refresh for **all** PDPs in the environment.

Publishes an OPAL data update instructing each PDP to immediately re-pull its
full authorization data, instead of waiting for the next periodic poll. Use
this to propagate external-data-source-backed changes in realtime.

`shard_id` is not accepted here: sharding is a per-PDP topology, so a single
shard target is meaningless across a heterogeneous environment. Target a shard
via the single-PDP endpoint (`POST .../configs/{pdp_id}/refresh`) instead.

post.description:
Rotates the API key of the PDP container with id `pdp_id`.

The rotation of the API key revokes the old API key and issues a new API key to the PDP.

For the per-environment Nexus PDP credentials row this rotates the environment's NATS
credentials instead of minting a token: every EdgePDP in the environment is revoked
and fresh bootstrap credentials are minted (PER-15666). That runs as an awaited
Celery task, so this call can take up to `NATS_ROTATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`.

post.description:
Copy environment

This endpoint either duplicates an existing environment to a new environment
in the same project, or copies from an existing environment to another
existing environment.

The `scope` object controls which objects will be copied to the target
environment.

To clone to a new environment, the user must have write permissions
to the containing project. To clone into an existing environment,
the user must have write permissions to the target environment, and,
with `delete_target_only_condition_sets`, permission to delete its
condition sets. In an environment protected by a policy guard, the copy
is refused with 403 when it would change or delete an object the guard
protects, and with 503 when the guard's decision point cannot be reached.

Copying environments across projects or organizations is not
allowed.

403.description: Nothing is written. The caller may not write to the target; with `delete_target_only_condition_sets`, may not delete condition sets in it; or the target is protected by a policy guard that forbids changing or deleting an object this copy would change (the refusal names the object)

406.description: Nothing is written. The source's condition-set hierarchy cannot be copied as stored: it holds a cycle, or a parent of another type or resource than its child; or, with `delete_target_only_condition_sets`, the target condition sets it would delete hold a cycle

409.description: Nothing is written. Another copy into the target is running; the target holds an object the copy would create and `conflict_strategy` is `fail` (the built-in resources `__user`, `__tenant` and `__role` merge instead: under `fail` a custom attribute of theirs both environments define with different types, an action of theirs whose attribute values differ, or a role both hold whose attribute values differ, null and {} counting as equal, or that would lose a permission is the conflict; the attribute check skips the tenant-association role's values, and a clone's new roles); under `fail`, the copy would replace the values of a role derivation both hold (its conditions or settings, or a shared rule's settings) or of an autogenerated condition set both hold (its conditions or parent; a clone's new target excepted); the target holds a condition set that cannot be reconciled with its source (another type, resource or autogenerated flag) under either strategy; a copied condition set's parent condition set is excluded by `scope`; a role derivation rule the copy would create names a related resource or role `scope` excludes, or a role permission it would create is on an action of a resource `scope` excludes; or `delete_target_only_condition_sets` would delete a condition set with a descendant that would not itself be deleted

503.description: Nothing is written. The target is protected by a policy guard, and the guard's decision point could not be reached to check an object this copy would change

post.description:
Copy environment

This endpoint either duplicates an existing environment to a new environment
in the same project, or copies from an existing environment to another
existing environment.

The `scope` object controls which objects will be copied to the target
environment.

To clone to a new environment, the user must have write permissions
to the containing project. To clone into an existing environment,
the user must have write permissions to the target environment, and,
with `delete_target_only_condition_sets`, permission to delete its
condition sets. In an environment protected by a policy guard, the copy
task fails with 403 when it would change or delete an object the guard
protects (the error is in the task's result), and the request itself
answers 503, enqueueing nothing, when the guard's decision point cannot be
reached.

Poll the task's result through this same environment.

Copying environments across projects or organizations is not
allowed.

tags.description:
The Organizations API gives you access to control and manage your Permit organizations.

An organization represents a **single billable account** (i.e: a company using Permit).
You may invite your team members to your Permit account, and thus multiple team members
may control an organization simultaniously (each member has access according to his role).
tags.name: Organizations

tags.description:
Customer self-service organization data export (PER-14389).

Async job: `POST /v2/data-export` starts a background export of the caller's own
organization; `GET /v2/data-export/{task_id}` polls it and, once ready, returns
a short-lived presigned download URL for the tar.gz (one CSV per table +
manifest). The org is derived from the API key (never a path/query parameter),
so a key can only ever export its own org.

Auth: an Organization API key with ADMIN access, because the archive contains
every plaintext API-key secret in the org. A write or read-only key is rejected
(403), exactly as it is on `GET /v2/api-key/{id}`.
tags.name: Data Export

tags.description:
Projects let you manage permissions for different business objectives from a single Permit account.

For example, you can create one project called "Billing App" and another project called "Web App".
Every project is a separate silo, and has its own unique set of environments and policies.
tags.name: Projects

tags.description:
Environments are silos contained within projects that enables you to safely iterate on changes.

Environments allow you to manage your policy throughout your entire development lifecycle,
from dev to production. Typical environments within a project could be `production`, `staging`,
or individual environments.

Each project must contain at least one environment.
You may clone an environment from a base environment, similar to git branches.
You can later safely merge the changes, after you tested them.
tags.name: Environments

tags.description: None
tags.name: Bulk Operations

tags.description:
Condition sets are sets of objects that are dynamically defined based on conditions on the objects' attributes.
Conditions sets allows you the flexibility of ABAC with the simplicity of RBAC.

There are currently two types of condition sets at the moment:
1) user set = the set of users that match all the specified conditions.
2) resource set = the set of resources that match all the specified conditions.

Examples:

- `us_based_employees` = {U1, ..., Un} = {all **users** who are *located in the US* and are *assigned the employee role*}
- `private_repos` = {R1, ..., Rn} = {all **resources** *of type repository* that *are private*}

We can then picture a **matrix** of assignment between *user sets* and *resource sets*.

Example:
If we check the checkbox where `us_based_employees` and `private_repos->clone` action intersect, we are setting a rule:
*all US based employees can clone private repos*.
tags.name: Condition Sets

tags.description:
Resource Action Groups are groups of actions that are assigned
to a role as one action.
tags.name: Resource Action Groups

tags.description:
Actions are the various ways you can interact with a resource or affect the resource.
Each (resource, action) pair defines a unique permission level.
tags.name: Resource Actions

tags.description:
Resource attributes allow you to specify an arbitrary schema attributes that are part
of the definition of resource and must be included in any of its instances.

Attributes are used to enforce attribute-based access control policies.

For example, if we are building the github's permissions system, we might want to know
on the `Repository` resource whether the repo is private or now. In such case we will
define a boolean `private` attributes that we can now use in our policies.
tags.name: Resource Attributes

tags.description:
Roles allow you to associate permissions indirectly via a job function.

Resource roles allow you to grant roles that are scoped to a resource, thus
expressing ownership or arbitrary relationships between an actor (i.e: user) and
a specific object.

This API allows you to manipulate roles: assign or unassign permissions to a role,
define hierarchy (inheritance) between two roles or define relationships between two roles.
tags.name: Resource Roles

tags.description:
Resources are *types* of objects or feature names that you wish to protect (or gate) with permissions.

For example, if you build a document-sharing app like google docs, you might want to define a "document" resource.

A resource definition block typically contains **actions**.
Actions are the various ways you can interact with the object / feature. Each (resource, action) pair defines a unique permission level.

A resource may also contain:
- roles (if you wish to define resource-bound roles or if your permissions model is relational)
- relations to other resources (if your permissions model is relational, i.e: you work with a ReBAC model)
- attributes (attributes that are typically defined on the resource, typically used in ABAC models)
tags.name: Resources

tags.description:
Roles allow you to associate permissions indirectly via a job function.

The Roles API allows you to manipulate roles: assign or unassign permissions to a role,
define hierarchy between roles or define relationships between resource roles.

Roles manipulated by this API are **tenant roles**, meaning when they are assigned, they are
assigned on a tenant.
tags.name: Roles

tags.description:
User attributes allow you to specify an arbitrary schema attributes that are part
of the definition of the User resource.

Attributes are used to enforce attribute-based access control policies.

*NOTE: A User is a Resource by itself, so basically a user's attribute is an attribute that assigned to the resource called "user".*

For example, if we are building the github's permissions system, we might want to know
whether the user is an owner of the organization or not. In such case we will
define a string `owner` attribute that we can now use in our policies.
tags.name: User Attributes

tags.description:
Users represent human end-users of your applications that you'd like to enforce permissions on.

You must create a user object in Permit.io prior to trying to enforce permissions for that user.
A user is identified by its key, and you can only create one user with the same key inside a Permit environment.
You can place users within tenants via role assignments in order to enforce multi-tenancy in your app.

You may create users via the API (shown below), with one of the SDKs, or via the Permit cloud console.
tags.name: Users

tags.description:
A tenant is a group of users that share a common organizational identity.

Each tenant is a silo that can enforce strict boundaries between your customers.
You can associate your protected objects with a specific tenant, and only users
belonging to that tenant may access these resources (pending on adequate permissions).

Usually, each tenant will represent one of the end-customer companies in your product
(i.e. the company that you sell to). Through the tenant feature we enable you to have
multi-tenancy straight out of the box.
tags.name: Tenants

tags.description:
Role Assignments are RBAC-constructs that state that a actor (i.e: user) is assigned a role within a tenant.

With role assignments you can assign or unassign roles to a user.
Role assignment define the relationship between users and tenants.
tags.name: Role Assignments

tags.description:
Represents a "mini" ABAC rule comprised of (UserSet, Action, ResourceSet).

If such tuple exists, it means all users matching the UserSet
can perform the Action on the resources matching ResourceSet.

Example:
(`us_based_employees`, `repository:clone`, `private_repos`) where:
- `us_based_employees` is a user set
- `repository:clone` is an action
- `private_repos` is a resource set
tags.name: Condition Set Rules

tags.description:
Resource instances are instances of resource types.

An instance represents **a single object** in your system on which you'd want to enforce authorization.
You can use this API to store tenancy data (tenant) and arbitraty data (attributes).
tags.name: Resource Instances
